nasa-tm-19700001369-comparison-of-tensil:
Alfred J. Nachtigall of Lewis Research Center compared two stainless steels in liquid helium in this October 1969 report. The alloys were 304L and 310S stainless steel. Both unnotched and notched specimens were tested, including welded notched pieces, with loading along and across the sheet rolling direction.

Yield strength for 310S ran nearly twice that of 304L. Ultimate tensile strength for 310S was about eighty percent of 304L in the unnotched condition. In notched tests, 310S strengths were significantly higher than 304L, welded or not. Limited tests at a still lower temperature showed no significant change. Cryogenic tanks and lines need exactly such low-temperature data.
uslaw-usc-t2-s190l:
Section 190l of Title 2 of the United States Code covers private claims pending before Congress and the taking of testimony. It sits in Chapter 6 of that title, on congressional and committee procedure and investigations. Any committee of either House with a private claim against the United States before it may order testimony to be taken. The committee must first be cleared to do so by the House that named it.

Under such an order, testimony may be taken before a standing master in chancery. Books and papers may be examined there, and copies of them proved there as well. The master must sit in the judicial district where the testimony is to be taken. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
